newsitem.title: India: Indian gilt prices down in light noon trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilt prices down in light noon trade.

text.p: Prices of government securities fell in thin noon trade on Wednesday as the market awaited details of a bond sale by the central bank, dealers said.
They said trade was light as market players were still uncertain of the amount of bids accepted by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
The RBI put the 12.59 percent 2004 government of India stock on sale earlier on Wednesday but stopped sales in late morning.
Dealers said bids for around 32 billion rupees had been accepted by the central bank.
"But it is not certain at the moment," said a dealer. "Trade will pick up only when we know for sure how much money has gone out of the system."
Dealers said the 12.14 percent 2000 stock was traded at 100.90 rupees against Tuesday's closing 101.20
"The 12.59 percent 2004 stock was earlier traded at 100.25 rupees but sellers are now quoting 100 rupees," said a dealer.
The 12.59 percent 2004 stock was auctioned on June 17 and rose to as high as 101.65 on Monday before the announcement of the bond sale by the RBI led to a fall in prices.
